To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of a liver-specific gene (C/EBP) is up-regulated during metamorphosis and is induced by thyroid hormone.
we have isolated two cDNA clones from Rana catesbeianna tadpole liver which encode C/EBP-like proteins.

the expression of a Rana catesbeianna liver-specific transcription factor, RcC/EPB-1, is up-regulated during spontaneous and thyroid-induced metamorphosis, and that the expression of RcC/EPb-1 mRNas precedes the expression of liver specific genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of genes and their products which are involved in tissue-specific changes in gene activity in the liver of the metamorphosing R. catesbeiana.
the identification and characterization of transcription factors that are important to the tissue-specific changes in gene regulation during amphibian metamorphosis.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the tissue-specific changes in gene transcription which occur in the liver during metamorphosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression and function of C/EBPs in the liver during metamorphosis are complex and require further studies.
C/EBP- related proteins may be a part of the molecular mechanism by which TH induces tissue-specific changes in gene transcription during metamorphosis in the tadpole.
RcC/EPB-1 and -3 are two different C/EPB genes that are expressed at different stages of metamorphosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned two genes that may play a role in the TH-induced metamorphoses of the tadpole's liver.
C/EBP- and thyroid hormone-related transcription factors may act in concert to induce a tissue-specific response during metamorphosis.
we have identified and characterized two members of the C/EBP family of proteins in the liver of the Rana catesbiana tadpole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thyroid hormone induces a number of liver-specific gene products in the tadpole liver.
we have isolated and characterized two C/EBP-like transcription factor genes, which are up-regulated in the liver of the R. catesbeiana frog during spontaneous and TH-induced larval metamorphosis.
the liver-specific changes in gene and protein expression that occur during metamorphosis can be induced precocciously by the administration of thyroid hormone to tadpoles.
